brief_criteria.SC1: verified URL forms for DOI and arXiv-ID lookup
brief_criteria.SC2: verified batch + paging mechanics sufficient for a 500-work corpus
brief_criteria.SC4: verified rate-limit numbers and pool/authentication requirement
brief_criteria.SC5: verified abstract reconstruction algorithm (or documented absence)
brief_criteria.SC7: license status confirmed with primary-source URL

claims.claim: mailto polite pool is dead: parameter ignored; API keys replaced it (pre-Feb 2026). Naive mailto-only clients get no pool benefit.

sources.quote: The mailto parameter is ignored.

claims.claim: Over budget or >100 req/s returns 429 (not 403). Official guidance is exponential backoff; no Retry-After documented on errors page.

sources.quote: Two things return 429 Too Many Requests: exceeding your daily budget, or making more than 100 requests per second.

claims.claim: Keyless free budget is only $0.10/day; free key is $1/day (10x). List+filter costs; single-entity gets are free. Corpus crawl burns list quota fast.

sources.quote: No key: "$0.10/day — a tenth of the above"

claims.claim: pyalex docs assert API key required from 2026-02-13; without key only 100 credits/day. Aligns with deprecation of mailto pool-stdlib scripts must carry api_key.

sources.quote: Starting February 13, 2026, an API key is required to use the OpenAlex API.

claims.claim: Large fraction of works lack abstracts: abstract_inverted_index coverage ~60% (2022) vs ~45% (pre-2000). Plan cannot assume abstract text for all papers.

sources.quote: over 60% of 2022 works vs. ~45% of pre-2000 works

claims.claim: No plaintext abstracts from API due to legal constraints; only inverted index. Rebuilding/redistributing abstract text has legal caveats beyond bare CC0 on metadata.

sources.quote: OpenAlex doesn't include plaintext abstracts due to legal constraints.

claims.claim: referenced_works is incomplete vs PDFs: unknown targets dropped, many Crossref records ship zero refs, non-DOI refs often fail match. Citation graph is biased/truncated, not capped by a stated N.

sources.quote: a work's referenced_works can be shorter than the reference list printed in its PDF.

claims.claim: Work ids object has no arxiv key (only openalex, doi, mag, pmid, pmcid). arXiv appears in indexed_in, not as first-class external id-naive ids.arxiv lookups break.

sources.quote: Work-specific keys: openalex, doi, mag (Microsoft Academic Graph integer ID), pmid (PubMed), pmcid (PubMed Central).

claims.claim: Singleton docs show OpenAlex ID and DOI only; no arXiv ID path. arXiv is a trusted ingest source, but arXiv-only (no DOI) resolve path is undocumented for /works/{id}.

sources.quote: Works' canonical external ID is DOI.

claims.claim: Duplicate works are merged; losers 301 to canonical. Clients that skip redirects or cache old W-IDs silently miss updates or double-count until merge.

sources.quote: 301 Permanent move — record merged; client should follow

claims.claim: display_name and title are the same string; every entity has display_name. Code branching on title-vs-display_name is wasted; null title handling still needed if select omits fields.

sources.quote: Both strings; the work's title. They are the same value.

claims.claim: concepts superseded by topics (still present, not maintained). New corpus code using concepts will rot; topics capped at three ranked entries.

sources.quote: Concepts are a superseded classification retained for continuity

claims.claim: select= allows root-level fields only; dotted nested paths error. No documented select×pagination interaction-do not assume select changes page caps.

sources.quote: Root-level fields only.

claims.claim: Basic paging hard-stops at 10,000 results; cursor can go deeper but bulk full /works crawl is discouraged (days, server load)-snapshot preferred over REST for corpus build.

sources.quote: Don't use cursor paging to download the entire dataset.

claims.claim: OpenAlex states full release under CC0 with no personal-use carve-out. Still, abstract plaintext is withheld for legal reasons-CC0 on dump ≠ free rein on reconstructed abstracts.

sources.quote: everything is released under a CC0 public-domain license, with no "personal use only" carve-out and no permission to ask.

claims.claim: Prior art wall: pyalex discards X-RateLimit-* headers and retries 429 without distinguishing per-second throttle vs daily credit exhaustion-stdlib should not copy that pattern.

sources.quote: No 429 handling or distinction between rate limiting and credit exhaustion

claims.claim: Inverted abstracts can carry trailing non-abstract junk (headings, keywords). Naive join of abstract_inverted_index pollutes local corpus text.

sources.quote: one can occasionally carry trailing text that isn't part of the abstract (section headings, keywords)

claims.claim: Removed fields still break old clients: host_venue, grants, has_ngrams already error. Stability risk if lit_fetch freezes a schema snapshot.

sources.quote: host_venue / alternate_host_venues on Works → use primary_location and locations

merge_note: Known contradiction to grade: arXiv resolution path. Scout claims /works?filter=ids.arxiv:1706.03762 succeeded (one probe); skeptic cites official attributes doc that the ids object has no arxiv key; digger's arXiv URL singleton form 404'd and its ids.arxiv probe 429'd. Also note: docs.openalex.org has moved entirely to help.openalex.org (all old doc URLs 301) - skeptic claims cite live help.openalex.org pages, so doc content was re-sourced there.
